lesson.title: Making New Knowledge Stick by Connecting It to Old: Elaborative Rehearsal
lesson.summary: Elaborative rehearsal is the process of linking new information to existing knowledge and meaning, which produces far more durable, well-organized long-term storage than simple repetition does.
lesson.body:
Elaborative rehearsal is the process of actively connecting new information to things a person already knows, rather than simply repeating it in its original form. Where maintenance rehearsal treats information as an isolated string of digits or words to be echoed back exactly as received, elaborative rehearsal asks what the new material means, how it relates to a personal experience, what it reminds a person of, or how it fits alongside other things already stored in memory.

This strategy works because it directly puts into practice the deep, semantic end of the levels of processing continuum described earlier. Recall that Craik and Lockhart's framework found that information processed for its meaning is retained far better than information processed only for its surface features or sound. Elaborative rehearsal is essentially a deliberate technique for guaranteeing that deep, semantic processing happens, rather than leaving it to chance. And because it weaves new material into a web of existing, related knowledge rather than storing it as an isolated fact, elaborative rehearsal builds many more possible paths back to that memory than repetition alone ever could, which is exactly the kind of well-organized, interconnected storage described in the discussion of memory storage as being far more stable and far easier to retrieve from later.

Consider a psychology student trying to remember that the amygdala, a small, almond-shaped structure deep in the brain, plays a central role in processing fear. Using maintenance rehearsal, she might simply repeat "amygdala, fear, amygdala, fear" to herself several times. Using elaborative rehearsal instead, she might think about why a structure positioned to react quickly, before slower conscious thought catches up, would make evolutionary sense for flagging danger, recall a specific moment of her own sudden fear response to a near car accident, and connect the amygdala to the broader fight-or-flight response she already learned about. Weeks later, on an exam, the maintenance-rehearsal version of this fact is likely to be gone or only vaguely familiar, while the elaborated version, tied to reasoning, personal memory, and a related concept, is far more likely to be fully retrievable, because any one of those connected threads can serve as a cue that leads back to it.

Elaborative rehearsal represents the capstone of this entire progression. Encoding strategies described the general project of shaping how information is processed as it enters memory; chunking, mnemonic devices, and spaced practice offered specific, well-studied techniques for doing that; and maintenance versus elaborative rehearsal describe the two broad routes information can take on its way into long-term storage. Maintenance rehearsal keeps information alive just long enough to use it, and can, with enormous repetition, eventually produce some durable learning, but elaborative rehearsal, by engaging meaning, connection, and organization from the very first encounter, is consistently the far more efficient and reliable path to the kind of stable, richly connected long-term storage that makes real learning possible.
